_doc: A2.9/A2.9a: diario de Dex (su móvil), capítulo 1 (outside). A3.3c: PIN partido (lámpara, tablón, nido, juntar mitades). A3.3d: DOORIS (tres factores), buzón (factura de Gerald + sobre) y felpudo pegado (tablón → Ledger). Formato y reglas en qa/README.md § Diario. Condiciones con la gramática de `when` de A2.6a: flag, !flag, item:id, !item:id; lista = todas. El puzle abierto «más avanzado» es el último de la lista cuyo openWhen se cumple y cuyo doneWhen no: por eso los hilos de DOORIS (felpudo, buzón, pregunta, llave) van después del PIN.

goals.text: Find Adrian's door code. It's in two halves, because of course it is.
Check Adrian's mail. Nosy is a job description.
Search the porch for anything Adrian hid.

notes.text: Behind the porch light, once it cooled down: half a note. '73..' The other half 'is with the birds. They never sell.'
Magpie nest, knocked down with a fence plank: the other half, wrapped in foil. '..14'. Kept the plank. Might need it.
Both halves taped together: 7314. 'If you found both halves, you're patient enough. — A.' He hid the code in two pieces. On purpose.
The front door has a name. DOORIS. Three-factor authentication: a PIN, a security question (the owner's best friend) and a hardware key. For a door.
Unknown number. 'A friend of Adrian.' Told me to be less of a stranger and hung up. Saved the number as 'Anon'.
Mailbox: a sealed envelope, 'CONFIDENTIAL — PATIENT ZERO'. Somebody important will want to see this.
Vet bill from the mailbox. Patient: Gerald. Species: rubber duck. Relationship: 'best friend'. Adrian's best friend is a duck. Noted. Literally.
Adrian's Ledger was glued under the HODL doormat. Took a plank to get it out. A hardware wallet under a doormat. Bold strategy.

hints: Moths know where the light is. So does whatever's behind it.
Hot bulbs don't burn anyone when they're off.
Use the porch light to switch it off. Then take what's behind it.
The birds know more than they let on.
Something long could reach that nest. Fences are made of long things.
Pull a plank off the fence. Poke the nest.
Two halves. One code. You can count to two.
You're carrying the whole code already. In pieces.
Use one half of the note on the other half.
You have numbers. Doors like numbers.
The keypad. The note. Introduce them.
Use the code note on the keypad.
Doors want keys. Adrian keeps his where everyone keeps everything.
The doormat. It's glued. Glue loses to leverage.
Use the fence plank on the doormat.
A best friend leaves a paper trail. Check the mail.
Adrian's mailbox. He never opened it. You can.
Open the mailbox. Read the vet bill.
A hardware key is useless in your pocket.
The Ledger. The keypad. Introduce them.
Use the Ledger on the keypad.
You know the name. The door doesn't. Yet.
Talk to the door. Answer with what the vet wrote.
Talk to the keypad. Pick the name on the vet bill.
